## Fish Islands in Antarctica: watching penguins on the northbound route

The [Fish Islands](/antarctica/place/fish-islands/) are a group of small islands and rocks near Prospect Point on the western coast of the Antarctic Peninsula. Cold waters, floating ice and steep shores surround them. On sea expeditions, the area is appealing for the opportunity to see colonies of Adélie penguins and Antarctic seabirds in their natural habitat.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} listing the Fish Islands as **an additional possible stop**. A visit is not tied to a guaranteed day or time. To observe the penguins, the vessel must be able to approach the colony area safely, and the crew must choose a permitted, accessible way to observe them.

## Which expedition includes the Fish Islands?

The island group is among the potential stops on the [13-day journey “Antarctica: Beyond the Antarctic Circle”](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-polar-circle-deep-south-13-days/). The expedition starts in Ushuaia, crosses the Drake Passage and explores the Antarctic Peninsula coastline. During the Antarctic portion, the ship aims to travel as far south as ice conditions permit.

On days 4–10, the Fish Islands remain **a possible stop on the return north**. Here, travelers may observe one of the southern colonies of Adélie penguins and Antarctic shags. A landing or Zodiac-based observation depends on the safety of the approach and the condition of approved visitor areas.

This differs from a guaranteed city or national-park excursion with regular access. On a polar expedition, the itinerary changes flexibly with the weather, drifting ice and wildlife movements. The journey remains rewarding even if a particular island must be replaced with another stretch of coastline.

## What wildlife can be seen around the islands?

The main natural attraction is **Adélie penguins**. These birds nest on rocky parts of the Antarctic shore and feed at sea. In season, their colonies can be especially busy: birds move between their nests and the water's edge, while their feeding routes extend through the surrounding waters.

Antarctic shags, seabirds and other animals typical of these waters may also be encountered around the Fish Islands. No particular species, population size or activity level can be promised in advance. Season and ice conditions influence bird behavior.

Observers should keep their distance and leave birds a clear route to the water. IAATO guidance calls for avoiding any action that changes wildlife behavior, as well as staying out of protected areas and not disturbing nests. Close-up photographs are best taken with an appropriate lens rather than by approaching a colony.

## Islands, Zodiac boats and ice conditions

The islands' small size and narrow rocky passages can make landings difficult. Sometimes watching from the water is easier and safer. A Zodiac can approach the shore only where conditions and rules permit, at a safe distance and with waves and floating ice taken into account.

| Element | What determines it |
|---|---|
| Penguin colonies | Wildlife season |
| Zodiac approach | Waves and ice |
| Shore landing | Safety and regulations |
| Day of visit | Crew decision |

The vessel's route may pass through ice-filled channels or change following the captain's assessment. For this reason, choose a cruise primarily for **the Antarctic expedition's overall geography and duration**, and treat the Fish Islands as an appealing extra possibility.

## How the Fish Islands differ from Detaille and Deception

The same 13-day itinerary may include [Detaille Island](/antarctica/place/detaille-island/), with its 1950s British scientific Base W. That stop is connected with the history of geological and mapping research. [Deception Island](/antarctica/place/deception-island/), by contrast, is known for its volcanic caldera and dark ash beaches.

The Fish Islands are especially interesting for birdlife and the marine environment. When comparing these places, there is little point in choosing the “most beautiful”: the attractions are different — penguins and birds, scientific heritage or volcanic scenery. A good expedition offers varied experiences, while weather determines the actual stops.

## Preparing for birdwatching

Antarctic wind makes the cold feel more intense even in summer. For a Zodiac outing, bring waterproof trousers and a jacket, warm layers, gloves and protection for camera equipment against spray. Binoculars help you watch wildlife without moving closer.

The expedition team gives a mandatory briefing before boarding the Zodiac. Follow the guides' instructions, leave no litter and do not feed wildlife. These rules apply whether or not you can go ashore and whether observation takes place entirely from the water.

## Frequently asked questions about the Fish Islands

### Where are the Fish Islands?

On the western side of the Antarctic Peninsula, near Prospect Point and the coast of Graham Land.

### Can you see Adélie penguins there?

They are one of the area's known species. Birds can be observed on shore and in coastal waters, but their presence at any specific spot and the chance of seeing them up close depend on the season and conditions.

### Is a landing included in the expedition price?

Listing the island group as a potential stop does not guarantee a landing. The expedition team determines how the area can be visited, while included services depend on the specific expedition offer.

### Which tours consider visiting the Fish Islands?

In our selection, the location is linked to the [13-day expedition beyond the Antarctic Circle](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-polar-circle-deep-south-13-days/) and mentioned as a possible stop on the return journey.

## Frei Station on King George Island: an air gateway to Antarctica

Frei Station, officially Presidente Eduardo Frei Montalva Base, is on the Fildes Peninsula of [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/) in the South Shetland Islands. This Chilean Antarctic base is operated by the Chilean Air Force. Its proximity to Teniente Rodolfo Marsh Airfield, which provides air connections to this part of Antarctica, is particularly important.

For travelers, the station is interesting mainly because of its role in transport. Participants in some expeditions fly here from mainland Chile, then travel to the shore and board a Zodiac boat that takes them to their vessel. This makes it possible to combine a flight across the Drake Passage with a sea journey along the Antarctic Peninsula.

## Teniente Rodolfo Marsh Airfield and weather restrictions

The airfield is on the ice-free part of Fildes Peninsula. Chile's civil aviation authority is responsible for air traffic control, meteorological services and flight safety. The airfield supports Antarctic research stations as well as tourist transport.

Having a runway does not mean flights operate on schedule regardless of the weather. Wind, cloud cover and visibility can affect takeoff, landing and the transfer to the ship. When choosing a fly-cruise, it is important to check the time allowance for flights and the conditions that apply if a departure is delayed.

## How Ada Tours uses Frei Station in its itinerary

The [“Classic Antarctica”](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/) itinerary starts with arrival in Punta Arenas and a pre-expedition briefing. A flight to King George Island is planned for the following day. After landing, travelers walk approximately 2 km through the area of Chile's Frei Station and [Russia's Bellingshausen Station](/antarctica/place/bellingshausen-station/), then transfer to a Zodiac and head to the expedition vessel.

Frei Station is therefore primarily part of **the transfer between aircraft and cruise ship**. Passing through the station area does not guarantee a visit inside its operational buildings. The itinerary then focuses on the [Antarctic Peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/), icebergs and possible shore landings, depending on conditions at sea.

| Stage | What to consider |
|---|---|
| Flight | Weather conditions |
| Walk across the island | Walking distance |
| Zodiac | Conditions on the water |
| Expedition cruise | Ice and landings |

## How Frei Station differs from Bellingshausen

Both stations stand on the same island but belong to different national programs. Frei is known for its aviation functions and airfield infrastructure. Bellingshausen is a Russian research station near the Orthodox Church of the Holy Trinity. One itinerary can pass both areas, but they are separate facilities with their own visitor rules.

If your main priority is spending as many days as possible among glaciers and on Zodiac outings, compare [Antarctica tours](/antarctica/tour/) by the length of their **sea-based portion**, rather than simply by whether they include a flight to Frei Station. You can also explore [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) when choosing a format.

## Frequently asked questions about Frei Station

### Where is Frei Station?

On Fildes Peninsula on King George Island in the South Shetland Islands, beside Teniente Rodolfo Marsh Airfield.

### Do all tourists fly to Antarctica via Frei?

No. Some itineraries use a fly-cruise route through King George Island, while others begin with a sea crossing of the Drake Passage.

### Can visitors enter the buildings at Frei Station?

Access to operational buildings requires permission. Passing through the station area as part of a cruise itinerary is not the same as taking a tour of the base.

### What happens if the weather prevents departure?

The exact arrangements depend on the conditions of the chosen itinerary and operator. Before booking, check flight rescheduling rules and allow extra time before your onward international flight.

## Tours via Frei Station: why travelers come here

[Frei Station](/antarctica/place/frei-station/) is a Chilean Antarctic complex on King George Island, one of the South Shetland Islands. Nearby is Teniente Rodolfo Marsh Martín Airfield, which receives flights from Punta Arenas. For travelers, this area often serves as the transfer point between an aircraft and an expedition ship.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through Frei Station on the main itinerary. The nature of this visit matters: **passing through the station area is not a guided visit to its research facilities**. The main expedition begins after the flight, when the group reaches the ship by Zodiac and continues its voyage.

## Classic Antarctica: an 8-day itinerary

[“Classic Antarctica”](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/) combines a flight to Antarctica with several days of cruising along the South Shetland Islands and the western coast of the Antarctic Peninsula. This format is called a fly-cruise: travelers fly over the stretch of open ocean that an ordinary seagoing expedition must cross.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_klassicheskaya_antarktida}}

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Punta Arenas | Arrival, briefing and start of the itinerary |
| King George Island | Flight, Frei Station and transfer to Zodiac |
| Antarctic waters | Expedition cruising and possible shore landings |
| Return | Flight to Punta Arenas, overnight stay and transfer |

The published itinerary lasts **8 days and 7 nights**. On the first day, participants arrive in Punta Arenas by the time specified in the program, attend a mandatory briefing and learn about the expedition arrangements. The flight to King George Island follows.

## What happens at Frei Station?

On King George Island, travelers encounter polar weather: strong winds, damp cold and rapidly shifting clouds are possible even in summer. The route from the airfield to the shore passes through the area of Chile's Frei Station and [Russia's Bellingshausen Station](/antarctica/place/bellingshausen-station/).

The “Classic Antarctica” program specifies an approximately **2 km walk** from the landing site to the shore. Travelers then board a Zodiac, which takes them to the expedition ship. This matters for people with limited mobility: before booking, check the requirements for walking, clothing and health, as well as what boarding assistance is available.

Frei Station and the nearby airfield provide essential logistics for the South Shetland Islands. The area is also involved in scientific and meteorological work. However, a route past research buildings does not grant permission to enter, photograph operational rooms or visit laboratories; any such visit must be arranged with station personnel.

## The onward journey to the Antarctic Peninsula

After leaving Frei Station, the seagoing portion of the expedition begins. The ship sails among icebergs and ice-filled fjords toward the shores of the [Antarctic Peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/). The program includes watching penguins, seals, whales and seabirds, as well as educational presentations aboard the ship.

Zodiac landings depend on wind, waves, ice conditions and the expedition team's decisions. Possible cruising areas include [Gerlache Strait](/antarctica/place/gerlache-strait/) and other Antarctic channels. As the weather window changes day by day, the precise set of shore stops may differ from the preliminary description.

In the final days, the vessel returns to the King George Island area. The group flies back to Punta Arenas, stays overnight in the city, and completes the program after breakfast and a transfer to the airport. The precise sequence remains dependent on flying and sea conditions.

## Fly-cruise or an expedition across the Drake Passage?

The main difference between a journey via Frei Station and many ocean expeditions is **how travelers cross the ocean between South America and Antarctica**.

A conventional sea route starts in Ushuaia and crosses the [Drake Passage](/antarctica/place/drake-passage/), where winds can create rough seas. A fly-cruise works differently: an aircraft from Punta Arenas takes travelers directly to King George Island, where the Antarctic sailing portion begins. This reduces time spent on the open ocean, but it does not eliminate boating trips, waves or weather delays within Antarctica itself.

For active sea itineraries, see [expeditions across the Drake Passage](/antarctica/place/drake-passage/tour/). For shorter fly-in journeys without a multi-day ship voyage, there are [itineraries featuring Collins Glacier](/antarctica/place/collins-glacier/tour/). These are different travel products even though they all use King George Island as a geographic point.

## Practical questions before booking

One of the biggest factors is **the flight's dependence on weather**. The plane may depart later than scheduled if conditions at King George Island's airfield deteriorate. Ask the organizer about delays and flight rescheduling, insurance requirements and the time allowance before your international flight home.

The second factor is physical fitness. This particular itinerary includes a two-kilometer walk to the Zodiac boarding point. The ground may be uneven and windy. Participants should be ready to move while wearing several layers of warm clothing and follow the guides' instructions when boarding.

The third question is which services are included. The published tour listing includes flights between Punta Arenas and King George Island, the organized expedition program, specified overnight stays and transfers. Check meal arrangements, additional expenses and available cabin categories in the [“Classic Antarctica” terms](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/).

## How to behave near an Antarctic station

Every part of a research station has an operational purpose. Antarctic regulations require visitors to respect scientific research, avoid interfering with equipment and enter facilities only with permission from responsible staff. Guides explain where visitors may go and how to move along the shore.

Penguins and other birds live around King George Island. They must not be fed, chased or approached so closely that their behavior changes. Conservation briefings take place before landings, and clothing and footwear are cleaned of possible contaminants when necessary. Read more about the expedition region in the [Antarctica section](/antarctica/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Frei Station a tourist attraction?

It is an operational Chilean Antarctic complex beside an airfield. On the tour described, travelers pass through the surrounding area to reach the shore; the itinerary does not include separate entry into scientific buildings.

### How do you get to Frei Station from South America?

[“Classic Antarctica”](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/) uses a charter flight from Punta Arenas to King George Island. Flying time is approximately 2 hours, but departure depends on weather.

### How far is the walk after landing?

Our program includes a walk of about 2 km through the Frei and Bellingshausen station areas to the Zodiac boarding point. If extended walking is difficult, check accessibility before booking.

### Do you have to cross the Drake Passage by ship?

No. The fly-cruise includes flights to and from King George Island. [Sea expeditions across the Drake Passage](/antarctica/place/drake-passage/tour/) reach the Antarctic Peninsula differently.

### Will we see whales and penguins?

Wildlife viewing is part of the expedition's purpose, but sightings depend on season, weather and animal behavior. The itinerary and possible landings may change.

### Is this tour suitable for a first visit to Antarctica?

It suits travelers who want to combine a short flight from Chile with several days of expedition cruising. Before choosing it, consider your health, shore-walking requirements, insurance and possible flight delays.

## Gerlache Strait in Antarctica: glaciers, whales and expedition-ship passage

[Gerlache Strait](/antarctica/place/gerlache-strait/) runs between the Palmer Archipelago and the western coast of the [Antarctic Peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/). It is a sea passage, not a designated landing site. Expedition-ship passengers encounter icy shores, islands, drifting ice and, with luck, marine mammals here.

The strait illustrates the difference between an Antarctic expedition and a conventional sightseeing itinerary. Weather, ice and the captain's decisions determine the ship's actual path. Even when Gerlache Strait is listed as a possible area, passage through it, a stop or a Zodiac outing cannot be guaranteed.

## Where is the strait and why is it interesting?

According to Antarctic geographic references, the strait separates the Palmer Archipelago from the shores of the Antarctic Peninsula. High islands surround it, including [Anvers](/antarctica/place/anvers-island/) and [Brabant](/antarctica/place/brabant-island/), while mountain slopes and glacier fronts line the mainland coast.

The name is connected with the Belgian Antarctic Expedition aboard the Belgica. In January and February 1898, the expedition explored this waterway; the strait was later named for its leader, Adrien de Gerlache. Today it is a geographic name for a marine navigation area, not the designation of a particular tourist pier.

An important distinction from the [Drake Passage](/antarctica/place/drake-passage/): Drake is an open-ocean crossing between South America and the Antarctic region, while Gerlache is a passage between islands and the peninsula's coast. Time spent in these two areas offers different experiences and calls for different planning.

## What happens while sailing through?

The main activity in the strait itself is observation from the ship. In the right light, passengers see contrasting stretches of dark water and ice, mountain ranges, glacial walls and individual icebergs. Some voyages may offer outings in small expedition boats if the route, weather and regulations allow it. But a boat excursion in a nearby bay does not amount to a guaranteed landing within the strait.

For each section, the captain and expedition team evaluate wind, visibility, ice conditions and the safety of approaches to shore. If a narrow channel is blocked by ice or swell makes an outing unsafe, the ship can take a different route. When planning a trip, the number of days in Antarctic waters and the expedition ship's real capabilities matter more than a long list of appealing names in a brochure.

## Why whales are seen here

During the Southern Hemisphere summer, humpback whales and other marine mammals feed in waters off the western Antarctic Peninsula. The International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO) has designated the Gerlache area for special measures to reduce the risk of vessel collisions with whales. This reflects regular sightings in these waters, but does not guarantee whales will appear beside any particular ship.

Wildlife watching here differs from visiting a penguin colony on [Ardley Island](/antarctica/place/ardley-island/). In Gerlache Strait, passengers generally see marine wildlife **from the water**. Chasing a whale for a photograph conflicts with responsible Antarctic visitation. The crew follows distancing and vessel-operation rules.

For travelers especially interested in marine life, it is worth comparing [Antarctic wildlife itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/antarctica/) and specific expedition dates.

## Gerlache Strait on Ada Tours itineraries

On the [8-day “Classic Antarctica” itinerary](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/), the flight from [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/) to [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/) is followed by a sea expedition around the South Shetland Islands and the peninsula's west coast. **Possible** cruising areas include Gerlache Strait, [Penola Strait](/antarctica/place/penola-strait/) and [Antarctic Sound](/antarctica/place/antarctic-sound/). The choice depends on weather and ice.

You are choosing an Antarctic Peninsula expedition with a flexible route, not a separately paid call at Gerlache Strait. When comparing [Antarctic cruises](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/antarctica/), consider the travel format, nights aboard the ship, opportunities for Zodiac outings and the rules for itinerary changes.

Extended expedition itineraries in the area may consider neighboring [Paradise Bay](/antarctica/place/paradise-bay/) and [Neko Harbour](/antarctica/place/neko-harbour/). Their presence in a destination catalog does not by itself mean they are part of your chosen cruise. Check the actual voyage map and potential landing sites in the specific program.

## Preparing for a day at sea

Even in summer, spending time on an open deck can mean wind, moisture and cold. Bring layered clothing, a waterproof outer layer, warm gloves and protection for camera equipment. Take precautions on a rolling deck and follow the crew's instructions.

When choosing a cabin and itinerary, consider susceptibility to seasickness, total time aboard and possible schedule changes. Allowing extra time after returning from Antarctica is especially useful if you have an independently booked international flight afterward.

## Frequently asked questions about Gerlache Strait

### Can whales be seen in Gerlache Strait?

Yes. The area is known for whale sightings, especially during expedition season. A sighting on any particular day is not guaranteed.

### Is Gerlache Strait a landing site?

No. It is a marine passage. If an itinerary includes shore visits, they take place on specific islands or coastal sites, rather than “in the strait” as a separate land destination.

### Do all Antarctic cruises sail through Gerlache?

No. Some routes may pass through this area, while others take different passages. Weather conditions change actual navigation even within a single itinerary.

### How does Gerlache differ from Penola Strait?

They are different sea passages off the western Antarctic Peninsula. Access to each depends on local ice conditions and the expedition team's decisions.

## Which tours pass through Gerlache Strait?

[Gerlache Strait](/antarctica/place/gerlache-strait/) lies off the western coast of the Antarctic Peninsula. Expedition ships sail here among snow-covered mountains, glaciers and drifting ice. In calm weather, passengers can admire the coastline and ice formations from the deck, and whales may be spotted in the water.

For travelers, the crucial difference is between **a strait on the map** and **a strait listed in an expedition program**: the ship's exact track is determined during the voyage. The vessel may enter Gerlache, take a neighboring channel or choose a different sheltered waterway. It is therefore more useful to compare itineraries by overall format, duration and how you reach Antarctica.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Gerlache Strait among the main route's destinations. We currently offer the [8-day “Classic Antarctica” fly-cruise](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/). In its expedition portion, the strait is listed as **one of several possible cruising areas**, alongside other waters off the peninsula.

## How the “Classic Antarctica” itinerary works

The journey begins in Punta Arenas, Chile. After meeting and preparing, participants fly to [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/) in the South Shetland Islands. From there, the group transfers to an expedition vessel and sets sail.

Key features of this itinerary:

- **8 days in the overall program.** It includes preparation in Punta Arenas, flights and the expedition portion around the Antarctic Peninsula.
- **A flight instead of a long sea crossing from South America.** The plane takes the group to King George Island, where the shipboard journey begins.
- **Several days on an expedition vessel.** The program includes Zodiac outings, bird and marine wildlife watching, and views of glaciers and icebergs.
- **Flexible geography.** Exploration days may take place around the South Shetland Islands, Antarctic Sound, Gerlache Strait or Penola Strait. The order and actual locations depend on weather and ice.

The expedition team makes daily decisions about the safest route. This matters especially along glaciated coasts: a narrow waterway visible on a chart does not mean a vessel can pass through it on every day.

Details of the duration, accommodation, included services and flight arrangements are in the [8-day cruise description](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/). Other options can be found in the [Antarctica tours catalog](/antarctica/tour/).

## Why sail into Gerlache Strait?

The strait is valued for the opportunity to observe **several defining features of maritime Antarctica at once**. From the deck, travelers can see sharply outlined mountains, glaciers descending to the sea and icebergs of different shapes. Sailing itself becomes an experience: light and mist quickly change the appearance of the same stretch of coast.

Another important attraction is marine mammals. The International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO) collects information about whale and seal sightings off the peninsula's west coast. Special speed restrictions apply in the Gerlache area where whales are regularly found. This shows how important the waters are for wildlife, but **a particular species cannot be guaranteed on any particular day**.

Travelers hoping to see whales should look for an expedition format with observation time on the water and access to open decks. For those most interested in snowy landscapes, itineraries with several days of cruising offer more opportunities to see different bays, fjords and forms of ice.

For trips focused on glacial scenery, explore the [“Nature”](/interests/nature/) section; for wildlife viewing, see [“Wildlife”](/interests/wildlife/); and for ship-based travel, see [“Cruises and Expeditions”](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/).

## Why passing through the strait is not a shore landing

Gerlache is primarily **a sea passage**. Cruise itineraries may identify it as a navigational area rather than a place where a landing is certain. Many bays and islands lie near the strait, but visitors can go ashore only when conditions are suitable and the rules at a particular site allow it.

Sea conditions, wind, drifting ice and the ability to operate Zodiac boats safely all influence the decision. One day, the expedition team may spend more time on the water; another day, they may arrange a landing at an accessible location. Treat listed stops as an expedition plan, not a scheduled transport service.

If your main goal is **to step onto Antarctic land**, compare the daily descriptions of specific potential landings. If you value glacial scenery from the water more, look at the number of expedition days and the overall cruising area. For Gerlache, these criteria are more useful than a promise to visit a named strait.

## Choosing an Antarctic cruise with the season in mind

Expedition ships operate during Antarctica's tourist season, when conditions are usually better than in the polar winter. Even in summer, however, the weather remains changeable. A single month or catalog photograph cannot tell you whether the ship will pass through Gerlache Strait.

Before booking, consider:

- **How you arrive.** A fly-cruise lets you start Antarctic sailing from King George Island; an expedition with an ocean crossing has different logistics and a different duration.
- **Number of days in Antarctica.** This influences how many areas might be visited under favorable conditions.
- **Exactly what the product includes.** Verify flights, the shipboard program, expedition outings and accommodation against the specific tour description.
- **Route flexibility.** The more an itinerary depends on a single bay or strait, the more important it is to understand weather-related alternatives.

Passengers must follow conservation rules: keep a safe distance from wildlife, avoid disturbing colonies and respect protected-site restrictions. The expedition team's instructions take precedence over a desire to approach a whale or step onto a striking icy shore.

## Questions about tours via Gerlache Strait

### Is passage through Gerlache Strait guaranteed?

No. In [“Classic Antarctica”](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/), it is listed as one of the expedition's possible cruising areas. The team chooses the actual track based on weather and ice conditions.

### Where is the strait relative to King George Island?

[King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/) is in the South Shetland Islands and is the starting point for fly-cruises. Gerlache lies farther south, off the western Antarctic Peninsula. On a single tour, these are separate stages of the journey.

### Can whales be seen during the passage?

Yes, encounters are possible: Gerlache waters are known for whale sightings. The species, number of animals and whether there will be any sighting cannot be determined in advance. Ships follow whale-protection measures, including speed limits in designated areas.

### Do you need special training for this cruise?

Special mountaineering skills are generally not needed to watch from the ship. However, you should consider boarding Zodiacs, potential landings on uneven ground, cold temperatures, swells and instructions from expedition personnel. Exact requirements depend on the trip.

### What if I want to see more areas of Antarctica?

Compare the number of expedition days and the shipboard program in [Antarctica tours](/antarctica/tour/). The wider the region covered and the longer the cruise, the more potential options the team may have, although weather can always change the route.
